title: The 10 Best Hacksaws
subtitle: High-tension, compact and mini hacksaws for cutting metal, PVC and bolts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A hacksaw holds a thin blade under tension for clean, controlled cuts in metal, pipe and bolts. We ranked 10 best-sellers from LENOX, Milwaukee, CRAFTSMAN, Klein Tools and value brands on rating, review volume and features (high-tension frames, flush-cut blade angles, spare blades and blade storage).

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 12-Inch Hacksaw (CMHT20138)

specs.extras: 4.375 in cutting depth, 90° and 180° blade angles

products.verdict: The most-reviewed hacksaw here: a solid metal frame that tensions the blade to 225 lb, with 90- and 180-degree blade positions for flush cuts, for about $10.
products.best_for: Homeowners who want one good hacksaw.
products.skip_if: You want spare blades in the box.

products.name: LENOX HT50 High-Tension Hacksaw

specs.extras: I-beam frame stores 5 blades; takes recip blades as a jab saw

products.verdict: The best-rated hacksaw here at 4.8 stars: an I-beam frame that tensions blades to 50,000 psi, stores five spares and doubles as a jab saw with reciprocating saw blades.
products.best_for: Plumbers, electricians and fabricators who cut metal often.
products.skip_if: You cut once a year; the CRAFTSMAN does fine.

products.name: Milwaukee 48-22-0050 12-Inch High Tension Hacksaw

specs.extras: Reinforced frame, stores up to 6 blades

products.verdict: Milwaukee's high-tension hacksaw with a reinforced frame, an easy high-leverage tension knob and storage for six spare blades.
products.best_for: Trades who want a pro saw for less than the LENOX.

products.name: Klein Tools 31430 High Tension Hacksaw with Heavy-Duty Frame and Jab Saw

specs.extras: Converts to jab saw tool-free, 45° and 90° mounting

products.verdict: A Klein hacksaw that tensions to 30,000 psi, mounts the blade at 45 or 90 degrees, and converts to a jab saw without tools.

products.name: LENOX Lightweight Hacksaw (1213188300)
products.verdict: A lighter LENOX frame that still tensions to 30,000 psi, with a front grip for two-handed cutting and a 45-degree position for flush cuts.
products.best_for: Anyone who wants LENOX quality for less.

products.name: AIRAJ 12-Inch High-Tension Hacksaw with 10 Spare Blades

products.verdict: A basic high-tension steel frame with a top-mounted knob, the cheapest full-size saw here.

products.name: KATA 10-Inch Mini Hacksaw with 3 Bi-Metal Blades
products.verdict: A compact aluminum mini hacksaw with two spare blades for light cuts in PVC, rod and bolts.

specs.extras: 12 in frame mounts at 90° or 45°; aluminum frames

products.verdict: Three hacksaws, full-size, compact and mini, plus eight spare blades including a double-sided wood/metal blade.

avoid.name: TOOLAN 8-in-1 Multi-Blade Hand Saw: Drywall, Hacksaw, Jab Saw and Wood Cutter
avoid.flag: No frame to tension a hacksaw blade
avoid.verdict: A handle that clamps short blades, sold as a hacksaw, though it has no frame to hold a blade in tension.
reasons: A hacksaw works because the frame pulls the blade tight. This tool holds blades by one end only, so a thin metal-cutting blade flexes and wanders instead of cutting straight.
It claims all eight blades are high-speed steel, including the drywall and wood blades, which are normally carbon steel.
If you want one tool that cuts metal and works as a jab saw, the LENOX HT50 and Klein 31430 are real high-tension hacksaws that convert to jab saws.

buyers_guide.a: A tight blade cuts straight and fast. High-tension frames (25,000 to 50,000 psi) keep thin blades from bending and wandering, especially in hard metal.
Use 18 TPI for thick, solid stock and 24 to 32 TPI for thin tubing and sheet. Keep at least three teeth in the material, and install the teeth pointing away from the handle.
A 12-inch frame cuts faster and straighter. Mini and compact saws reach into cabinets and tight spaces where a full frame won't fit.
Mounting the blade at 45 or 180 degrees lets you cut a bolt or pipe flush with a surface.
Bi-metal blades combine hard teeth with a flexible back, so they last longer and resist shattering. They're worth the small extra cost.
